summary: The last 4 weeks reveal a heavily fatigued athlete: sleep is chronically short (multiple nights under 5 hours, one night at 41 minutes), body battery has been critically low (2–31 on several recent mornings), and training volume has been sporadic with a dangerous HR spike on July 18 (avg 179 bpm running). The one positive is the July 20 long ride (77km) showing baseline cycling fitness exists, and open-water swims are building toward the Half Oceanman target. Immediate priority must be rebuilding sleep and recovery before any structured training load can be absorbed.
suggestions: Enforce a strict body battery gate of ≥45 before any session through at least August 8 — if the gate is not met, full rest only, no 'consolation' walks or easy spins that still add stress.

Target 7+ hours in bed every night this week regardless of sleep quality achieved — the pattern of 41-minute, 163-minute, and 183-minute nights is clinically significant and will prevent any training adaptation until corrected.

The Half Oceanman swim (5,000m at 2:30/100m) in 63 days is the priority race: begin rebuilding pool volume systematically from August 4 with technique-focused sessions, targeting 3×/week swimming by August 18 to restore feel after the 4-week open-water-only period.
The July 18 run at avg 179 bpm (training load 208) was a red-flag session — avoid any running above HR 145 until at least August 9, and gate all runs on morning body battery ≥50 to prevent a repeat.

For the Treviso 10K (71 days away), begin adding 4–5 × 1km race-pace intervals at 5:45/km in week 9 (August 20 onwards) only after sleep and body battery metrics normalise — the current fitness base supports this pace but only when recovered.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk7 Evening session — 30 min at 210–244W with body battery gate ≥50
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Full rest or 20-min gentle walk only — do not attempt the cycling session; given body battery of 0–31 across July 30–August 1 and less than 5 hours sleep on multiple recent nights, even a Z1 spin is counter-productive this day.
proposed_changes.reason: Body battery has been critically depleted (0 on Aug 1, 25 on July 28) and sleep is severely insufficient — no cycling stimulus will be absorbed and additional stress risks compounding fatigue into the Half Oceanman build.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk7 Long Ride — 60–75 min Z1–low-Z2 at 128–145W, treat as systems check
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 45-min flat Z1 spin capped at 128W maximum — only execute if morning body battery is ≥55 AND sleep averaged ≥6 hours for August 4–7; otherwise replace with a 30-min easy walk. Drop the 84km distance target entirely this week.
proposed_changes.reason: Recovery from the severe sleep deficit of late July will not be complete by August 8, so a hard cap on both duration and power protects against compounding fatigue entering the critical Half Oceanman build weeks.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk8 Long Ride — 92km at 128–177W (Z2 endurance), 240 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 70–90 min at 128–160W (low Z2), flat route, no distance target — add Z3 tempo blocks only if morning body battery is ≥60 AND sleep averaged ≥6.5 hours for August 11–14; cap at 100 min absolute maximum.
proposed_changes.reason: Jumping to a 240-min ride in week 8 after the severe depletion of late July is too aggressive; a gated, shorter ride maintains fitness stimulus while protecting the athlete from overreach heading into the Half Oceanman peak block.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk9 Pool Swim (Friday) — 60 min, 2,500m with 3×600m @ 2:25/100m race-simulation set
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 60 min pool session: 2,500m total — 400m warm-up, 3×600m @ 2:25–2:30/100m with 45-sec rest (extend rest to 60 sec if pace slips beyond 2:35/100m), 300m cool-down; this is the first true Half Oceanman race-pace rehearsal, so prioritise pacing control over speed.
proposed_changes.reason: With the Half Oceanman 5,000m swim as the nearest race priority, this session must anchor race-pace rehearsal at 2:30/100m — structured with appropriate rest intervals given the athlete is returning from a predominantly open-water-only swim block.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk16 Pool Swim (Friday) — 60 min pool session, 2km+, pace ≤2:30/100m
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Rest day — no swimming 2 days before the Treviso 10K race; at most a 10-min gentle shakeout jog in the evening with 4×100m strides at race pace (5:45/km) to stay loose, followed by race-day prep routines.
proposed_changes.reason: A 60-min swim session 2 days before the Treviso 10K creates unnecessary fatigue in the upper body and disrupts taper — mandatory pre-race scheduling conflict resolution.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk16 Long Ride — 240 min cycling session the day before Treviso 10K
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Full rest day — absolutely no cycling the day before a 10K race; optional 15-min easy walk in the morning for leg activation only, race-day kit preparation and nutrition planning instead.
proposed_changes.reason: A 240-minute ride the day before the Treviso 10K would catastrophically compromise race performance — mandatory pre-race scheduling conflict resolution, athlete safety takes absolute priority.
